current_answer: Current evidence supports seven distinct routes: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted context-carrying WebRTC session; Yoroll says H3 Superfast powers YoLive, a public group proposal-and-vote route for the next scene; Reactor FastH3 is a high-end VSA queue-and-playout route; FastVideo has local FastH3 clip paths; a community project reports one RTX 5090 sustaining an unattended dense FastH3 channel at 22.1 fps through 448×448 output, prequeued prompts, and retimed playout; Comfy’s optimized H3 path broadens local access; and vLLM-Omni documents a separate OpenAI-compatible H3 service for T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA. A new FastH3 8-Step V2 Comfy package is the actionable local update: FastVideo documents a fixed eight-forward V2 recipe, but FastVideo calls it T2AV-only while a current official ComfyUI template says it also accepts first/last-frame FL2VA. Treat the scope as unresolved until a pinned run settles it.

catalogue_card.question: Can FastH3’s new ComfyUI path anchor your next scene?
catalogue_card.text: FastVideo calls 8-Step V2 text-to-video only. A current ComfyUI template says the same checkpoint also accepts first and last frames. Do not promise a transition until a pinned run settles the scope.

summary: FastVideo released FastH3 8-Step V2 as a distinct eight-forward DMD2 MiniMax H3 checkpoint; its older FastH3 Preview path remains four-forward.
A current official ComfyUI template links a Comfy-layout V2 package and says it supports T2VA plus first/last-frame FL2VA, while excluding Ref2VA.
FastVideo’s own current schedule page calls V2 T2AV-only. The scope conflict makes a first/last-frame transition an unverified claim, not a workflow promise.
No current V2 source inspected here provides a pool-measured or comparable local result for quality, hardware fit, time-to-ready, cost, failures, queue capacity, continuous delivery, or interaction.
uncertainty: FastVideo and ComfyUI conflict on the FastH3 8-Step V2 input scope. The pool did not run either T2VA or FL2VA, or measure quality, time, hardware fit, price, queueing, or failures.
The one-RTX-5090 FastH3 channel is a community project’s one-machine self-report; the pool has not run or independently audited it, and its downloadable files are access-gated.
Reactor’s playout, continuity, and four- or eight-B200 timing statements are project-maintainer documentation for one implementation, not independent pool measurements or a viewer study.
fal’s current endpoint terms and continuity behavior are provider claims; a prior provider learning article still conflicts on session and audio details.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
Yoroll’s YoLive control loop and H3 Superfast timing are company launch claims; the pool did not observe a live vote, measure end-to-end response, or independently reproduce the eight-B200 result.

vLLM-Omni’s H3 serving and four-B300 result are maintainer documentation for one warmed full-H3 FL2VA workload; the pool has not operated it or measured cost, quality, queueing, failure behavior, or client-to-visible latency.
freshness_note: Checked 18 September 2026. FastH3 8-Step V2 now has a current ComfyUI package and template, but FastVideo and ComfyUI conflict on whether first/last-frame FL2VA is supported. The pool has not run the route.
